title.rendered: The Iris Prize 2026 – LGBTQ+ Film Festival

content.rendered: The Iris Prize is the world’s largest LGBTQ+ short film prize. The best international short wins £30,000 and the best British or Irish short wins £10,000. Films must be under 40 minutes and completed within the last two years. Submissions accepted via FilmFreeway.

content.rendered: HTW Berlin’s IUNO project is an EU-funded research initiative supporting artists at the intersection of AI and XR. The selected artist or team will co-develop a project at HTW Berlin from May 2026 to January 2027, with access to equipment, mentorship, a scientific paper publication, and public networking events.

title.rendered: Anthropic AI Safety Fellows Program (May or July 2026 Cohorts)

content.rendered: A four-month, full-time paid research fellowship in empirical AI safety. Fellows receive mentorship, a weekly stipend, and funding for compute and research expenses. Participation is available remotely in the US, UK, or Canada, with optional shared workspaces in Berkeley and London.

title.rendered: OCEANS Open Call – MIT Museum (Public Programs)

content.rendered: The MIT Museum is seeking proposals for innovative public programs exploring humanity’s relationship with the theme of OCEANS, in support of the museum’s mission to blend art, science, technology, and design. The open call runs from December 5, 2025 to February 5, 2026, alongside the museum’s upcoming OCEANS theme launching in September 2026.

content.rendered: The Morgan Drawing Institute and the Menil Drawing Institute (Houston) offer a 3-9 month research fellowship supporting independent projects on the history, theory, interpretation, or cultural meaning of drawing. The Morgan-Menil Fellow is expected to spend part of the fellowship in residence at The Morgan Library & Museum (New York) and another part at the Menil Collection, with time devoted primarily to the research project and participation in Drawing Institute programs. Stipend is commensurate with experience: $4,000/month (pre-doctoral), $4,850/month (post-doctoral within seven years of PhD), or $5,100/month (mid-career), plus a modest travel allowance. Application deadline: December 15, 2025.

title.rendered: Bobby Anspach Studios Foundation Grant Program

content.rendered: The Bobby Anspach Studios Foundation invites proposals from visual artists creating work that fosters human connection and climate consciousness. In its inaugural year, the foundation will award two $50,000 major grants and three $8,000 emerging artist grants (unrestricted awards, no application fee). Application deadline: December 30, 2025 (11:59 PM EST).

title.rendered: VIVERSE Creator Program – Creator Grants for WebXR Worlds

content.rendered: VIVERSE’s Creator Program offers creator grants to help developers, artists, and storytellers build web-based 3D immersive experiences, including interactive worlds, immersive art, and next-gen games and storytelling. The program highlights support for building, testing, and deploying across mobile, desktop, and VR, with creator resources and community support. Apply via the VIVERSE Create portal.

content.rendered: The Folger Institute offers long-term fellowships for the 2026-2027 academic year, providing $70,000 for a standard 9-month period to support full-time scholarly work drawing on the Folger’s collections and programs. Fellows may take up to 3 months virtually as part of the fellowship schedule. Applications are due December 15, 2025 (11:59 PM ET).

Fellows may take up to 3 months virtually as part of the fellowship schedule. Applications are due December 15, 2025 (11:59 PM ET).

title.rendered: Not Your Grandma’s Gallery – Open Call for Artists (The Holy Art)

content.rendered: The Holy Art Gallery’s “Not Your Grandma’s Gallery” is an ongoing open call series for artists worldwide, positioned as high-energy, contemporary exhibitions across different cities. Listings typically note exhibition dates and a deadline to apply that may be marked as TBC depending on the edition. Check the current call page/post for the specific city, exhibition dates, and the latest submission deadline.

title.rendered: NewImages Festival 2026 – XR Competition Call for Projects

content.rendered: NewImages Festival (Paris) is calling for XR projects for its XR Competition, open to VR, AR, mixed reality, narrative video games, hybrid performances, and other innovative formats. Eligible works are completed in 2025 or by March 2026 (no premiere required). Selected projects are showcased at the festival and can compete for awards including the Grand Prize (6,000€) and Impact Award (3,000€). Call open until January 8, 2026. Festival runs April 8-12, 2026 at la Cité des sciences et de l’industrie.

yoast_head_json.og_description: NewImages Festival (Paris) is calling for XR projects for its XR Competition, open to VR, AR, mixed reality, narrative video games, hybrid performances, and other innovative formats. Eligible works are completed in 2025 or by March 2026 (no premiere required). Selected projects are showcased at the festival and can compete for awards including the Grand Prize (6,000€) and Impact Award (3,000€). Call open until January 8, 2026. Festival runs April 8-12, 2026 at la Cité des sciences et de l'industrie.

content.rendered: Meaningful XR (MXR) invites submissions for its 2026 conference. The event runs May 30-31, 2026 in Portland, Oregon, with hybrid options for posters and remote participation in selected sessions and social events (via headset, computer, or mobile). Physical attendance of at least one author is required for papers, panels, and demos. Submission deadline: February 20, 2026. Decisions announced April 1, 2026.
